style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Almost certainly not a separate composition but the third stanza of Psalm 42 -- no title, the same refrain, the same exile far from the altar. The complaint has not moved: You are the God who is my stronghold, so why have You rejected me, why do I walk about in mourning because of the enemy's oppression? What is new is the prayer. Send out Your light and Your truth -- two of God's attributes dispatched as escorts -- and let them lead me back to Your holy mountain, to the altar, to God who is the gladness of my joy, where I will thank You on the harp. Then the refrain a third time, and the only time the poet gets to end on it: why are you bowed down, O my soul? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance and my God. The soul is talked to until it agrees.

1.text: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against a nation without covenant loyalty; from the man of deceit and injustice rescue me.
1.amp: Judge [shaphat -- vindicate] me, O God [Elohim], and plead [rib -- contend] my cause [rib -- case] against an ungodly ['unmerciful', lo-chasid, the KJV margin] nation [goy]: O deliver [palat] me from the deceitful ['a man of deceit and iniquity', mirmah avlah, the KJV margin] and unjust man.
1.notes: shophteni Elohim ve-ribah ribi (H8199, H430, H7378, H7379): judge me and CONTEND my contention -- rib, the lawsuit word, doubled -- mi-goy lo-chasid (H1471, H2623): from a nation 'not chasid', without covenant loyalty, the margin's 'unmerciful'; me-ish-mirmah ve-avlah tephalleteni (H376, H4820, H5766, H6403): from a man of deceit and injustice bring me out. Psalm 43 has no title, and the shared refrain makes it almost certainly the third stanza of Psalm 42 -- one poem, one refrain, three verses of it.

2.text: For You are the God who is my stronghold; why have You rejected me? Why do I walk about in mourning because of the enemy's oppression?
2.amp: For You are the God [Elohim] of my strength [maoz -- stronghold]: why do You cast me off [zanach -- reject]? why go [halak] I mourning [qadar -- in dark clothes] because of the oppression of the enemy [oyeb]?
2.notes: ki-attah Elohe mauzzi lamah zenachtani (H430, H4581, H2186): You are the God of my stronghold -- WHY have You cast me off? -- the same two facts held together that Psalm 42:9 held ('my rock ... why have You forgotten me'); lamah-qoder ethallekh be-lachats oyeb (H6937, H1980, H3906, H341): why do I walk about qoder, darkened, in mourning dress, under the enemy's squeeze? Psalm 42:9's line repeated nearly word for word: the complaint has not moved.

3.text: Send out Your light and Your truth; let them be the ones to lead me; let them bring me to Your holy mountain and to Your dwellings.
3.amp: O send out [shalach] Your light [or] and Your truth [emeth]: let them lead [nachah] me; let them bring [bo] me unto Your holy [qodesh] hill [har], and to Your tabernacles [mishkan -- dwellings].
3.notes: shelach-orekha va-amittekha hemmah yanchuni (H7971, H216, H571, H5148): send Your light and Your truth -- 'THEY shall lead me': two of God's attributes dispatched as escorts, the way goodness and covenant love follow in Psalm 23:6; yebiuni el-har-qodshekha ve-el-mishkenotekha (H935, H2022, H6944, H4908): let them bring me to Your holy mountain and Your dwellings. The exile of Psalm 42:6 (Hermon, the Jordan) asks for a guided walk home.

4.text: Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, the gladness of my joy, and I will thank You on the harp, O God, my God.
4.amp: Then will I go [bo] unto the altar [mizbeach] of God [Elohim], unto God [El] my exceeding joy ['the gladness of my joy', simchah gil, the KJV margin]: yea, upon the harp [kinnor -- lyre] will I praise [yadah -- thank] You, O God [Elohim] my God [Elohim].
4.notes: ve-aboah el-mizbach Elohim (H935, H4196, H430): and I will come to the altar of God -- the goal of the pilgrimage Psalm 42:4 remembered. el-El simchat gili (H410, H8057, H1524): to God, 'the gladness of my joy', the margin's literal: joy stacked on joy, and God Himself the object of it; ve-odekha be-khinnor Elohim Elohai (H3034, H3658, H430): and I will thank You with the lyre, O God, my God. The doubled name is the prayer's whole answer: 'my God' after 'why have You cast me off'.

5.text: Why are you bowed down, O my soul? Why do you roar and churn within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
5.amp: Why are you cast down [shachah -- bowed low], O my soul [nephesh]? and why are you disquieted [hamah -- in an uproar] within me? hope [yachal -- wait] in God [Elohim]: for I shall yet praise [yadah -- thank] Him, who is the health [yeshuah -- salvation] of my countenance [panim], and my God [Elohim].
5.notes: mah-tishtochachi naphshi u-mah-tehemi alai (H7817, H5315, H1993): why bowed low, my soul, and why the roar inside me -- hamah, the sound of the sea and of a crowd. hochili l-Elohim ki-od odennu (H3176, H430, H3034): HOPE in God, for I shall yet praise Him. yeshuot panai v-Elohai (H3444, H6440, H430): the salvations of my face, and my God. The third and last time the refrain of Psalm 42:5, 11 is sung, and the only one the poet gets to end on: the soul is talked to until it agrees.
